record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.original_question: Given a continuous graph Γ, can one bound its radius-1/2 chromatic number χ_{1/2}(Γ) above and below using the chromatic number χ(G(Γ)) of the associated combinatorial graph together with the number n of endpoint vertices? More broadly, can one derive useful upper and lower bounds for χ_{1/2}(Γ) from other graph parameters that are computable in polynomial time?

evidence.quote: Regardless computational complexity, an interesting question to address is: Given a continuous graph Γ, can one specify a lower and an upper bounds for χ1/2(Γ) in terms of a function of χ(G(Γ)) and n? Any other bounds for χ1/2 as functions of other (especially, polynomial-time computable) parameters are also very much interesting.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A continuous graph Γ is a topological space obtained from a finite simple combinatorial graph G(Γ) = (V,E) (with |V| = n endpoint vertices) by replacing every edge e = {u,v} ∈ E by a rectifiable arc of unit length whose endpoints are u and v; distinct arcs intersect only at common endpoints. Distances in Γ are measured along these arcs (the intrinsic metric), so each point of Γ lies either on a vertex or on the interior of some unit-length edge.

For a real number r > 0, an r-ball B(x,r) ⊂ Γ is the set of points of Γ at intrinsic distance ≤ r from x. A finite collection of r-balls 𝓑 = {B(x_1,r), …, B(x_m,r)} is an r-cover of Γ if its union equals Γ. Given an r-cover 𝓑 and a positive integer c, a proper c-coloring of 𝓑 is a function f: 𝓑 → {1,…,c} such that f(B(x_i,r)) ≠ f(B(x_j,r)) whenever B(x_i,r) ∩ B(x_j,r) ≠ ∅. The continuous graph Γ is (r,c)-colorable if some r-cover of Γ admits a proper c-coloring. The radius-r chromatic number is
  χ_r(Γ) := min{ c ∈ ℤ_{>0} : Γ is (r,c)-colorable }.

Let χ(G(Γ)) denote the ordinary chromatic number of the underlying combinatorial graph G(Γ).

Problem. Specialize to r = 1/2.
(a) Determine functions L(χ(G(Γ)), n) and U(χ(G(Γ)), n) — preferably as tight as possible — such that for every continuous graph Γ with n endpoint vertices,
  L(χ(G(Γ)), n) ≤ χ_{1/2}(Γ) ≤ U(χ(G(Γ)), n).
(b) More generally, exhibit nontrivial upper and lower bounds for χ_{1/2}(Γ) in terms of polynomial-time computable parameters of G(Γ) (e.g., maximum degree, clique number, treewidth, etc.).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a 2025 survey on combinatorial properties of continuous graphs. No subsequent work establishing such bounds for the radius-1/2 chromatic number χ_{1/2}(Γ) in terms of χ(G(Γ)), n, or other polynomial-time-computable parameters was located.
